Pile cap
Placed under an individual column: a reinforced concrete block distributes the column load to the pile group below it. The pile reinforcement is anchored into the cap.
Grillage (pile grillage)
Under walls and rows of columns: the pile heads are tied together by reinforced concrete beams, and the load of the wall reaches the piles through the beam.
Slab (piled raft)
Under large, uniformly loaded buildings – for example towers and underground car parks: the reinforced concrete slab works together with the piles and also transfers load to the soil.

Quiz – what is a deep foundation?
What fundamentally distinguishes a deep foundation from a shallow foundation?
Besides its base, it can also transfer load to the soil along its shaft (side).
It always reaches at least 10 m deep.
It can only be made of precast elements.
It needs no structure tying its heads together.
A deep foundation is a load-transferring element between the structure and the deeper bearing stratum that transfers load at its base and along its shaft.
Which is NOT a typical reason for a deep foundation?
The bearing stratum is directly below ground level.
A shallow foundation would produce unacceptable settlement.
There is a risk of scour around the bridge pier.
The reliable bearing stratum lies only deeper.
If the good layer is directly below the surface, a shallow foundation is usually the simplest and cheapest solution.
What are the three main types of deep foundation?
Pile foundations, diaphragm wall foundations, well and box foundations
Strip foundations, rafts, pile foundations
CFA, Franki pile, jet grouting
Soil replacement, preloading, piling
Today pile foundations are built most often; diaphragm walls are used mainly for excavation support, and well and box foundations are increasingly rare.
What is an excavated block foundation?
A transitional solution: a block excavated without support and concreted immediately, in cohesive soil to approx. 5–6 m.
A precast reinforced concrete block driven into the ground.
A diaphragm wall panel made with bentonite slurry support.
The reinforced concrete grillage tying the pile heads together.
A “transitional” solution between shallow and deep foundations, also called a well foundation in Hungarian practice.
For a wind turbine, what governs the design of the foundation?
The tilt of the tower: the allowable differential settlement is approx. 3 mm/m.
The chemical aggressiveness of the groundwater.
The weight of the blades.
The depth of frost penetration.
For tall, slender towers even a small differential settlement causes significant tilt.
What does the pile foundation of a new structure consist of?
The piles and the cap, slab and/or grillage tying their heads together.
Only the piles – the superstructure rests directly on them.
The piles and the grout injected around them.
A strip footing with a layer of replaced soil below it.
The connecting structure distributes the load and makes the piles work together.
Which is NOT a reason why more and more deep foundations are built today?
The standards no longer allow shallow foundations.
Buildings with ever larger loads and greater sensitivity to settlement are being built.
We increasingly have to build on filled, marshy sites.
Deep foundation technologies have become competitive.
Shallow foundations are still fully accepted today – where suitable, they are often the cheapest.
Why is a bridge pier standing in a river bed placed on piles?
Because the scour hole around the pier can reach the base of a shallow foundation, whereas the piles reach below the scour depth.
Because the shallow foundation would float up due to buoyancy.
Because piles do not corrode in water.
Scour is one of the most common causes of bridge damage – that is why river piers get deep foundations.
The piles of the Burj Khalifa (828 m) are shorter than the foundation elements of the Petronas Towers (452 m). What is the main reason?
The depth of the foundation is set primarily by the subsoil, the depth of the bearing stratum.
A taller building is always lighter.
There is no groundwater in Dubai.
The Burj Khalifa was built on a diaphragm wall.
It is often not the height (load) of the building but the soil that decides how deep the foundation has to reach.
